changed.title: A 100(k+1)^3 times 2^(7r) gate ceiling for the r-round common-key test on two k-bit names when 14r ≤ k, using fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : Nat), 5 ≤ k → (k % 6 = 1 ∨ k % 6 = 5) → 14 * r ≤ k →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let h := (k + 1) / 2
  let graph : Fin (2 ^ k) → Fin (2 ^ k) → Bool := fun row col =>
    (List.range (2 ^ k)).any (fun w =>
      decide (first w row.val < 2 ^ (k - h)) && decide (second w col.val < 2 ^ (k - h)))
  let budget := 100 * (k + 1) ^ 3 * 2 ^ (7 * r)
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (k + k) C ∧
    C.size ≤ budget ∧
    ∀ bits : Fin (k + k) → Bool,
      C.eval (List.ofFn bits) = PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) graph bits
changed.unlocks: Uses L-clb-044 to bound the decision circuit on the two names for the few-round rule, including three rounds.
changed.context: Trace each tested bit back to the key. Both tests at two or more rounds fit in one interval of diameter at most 7r. The tested positions are consecutive, so their union has at most ceil(k/2)+7r distinct positions when 14r <= k. Cut there. Carry one reachability wire per suffix, append either bit, test the local window and OR its two predecessors. Keep the names as inputs and hardwire the window for each guard. At one round stagger the tests by one place. At zero rounds compare the overlapping name bits.

At one round stagger the tests by one place. At zero rounds compare the overlapping name bits.

changed.title: A fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit for existential constraints on overlapping windows of a binary word with free ends
changed.statement:
∀ (n t d b : Nat)
  (guard : Fin t → Nat → (Fin n → Bool) → Bool),
  (∀ (i : Fin t) (pattern : Nat), pattern < 2 ^ (d + 1) →
    ∃ G : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo G ∧
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack n G ∧
      G.size ≤ b ∧
      ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, G.eval (List.ofFn x) = guard i pattern x) →
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack n C ∧
    C.size ≤ 2 ^ d * (t * (2 * b + 3) + 1) + 2 ∧
    ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (C.eval (List.ofFn x) = true ↔
      ∃ word : Fin (2 ^ (t + d)), ∀ i : Fin t,
        guard i ((word.val / 2 ^ i.val) % 2 ^ (d + 1)) x = true)
changed.unlocks: Turns local guard circuits into one decision circuit when the tested interval fits within the key.
changed.context: Carry one wire per d-bit suffix. Initially every suffix is possible. At each position copy the test circuit for each (d+1)-bit pattern, AND it with the wire for its low d bits, and OR the two answers for each successor suffix. Induct on positions by appending or deleting one bit. OR all final wires. Charge two tests, two ANDs and one OR per suffix per layer. Keep public input indices fixed when copying gates and map any missing output to a shared false wire.

At each position copy the test circuit for each (d+1)-bit pattern, AND it with the wire for its low d bits, and OR the two answers for each successor suffix. Keep public input indices fixed when copying gates and map any missing output to a shared false wire.

changed.title: The trace of a binary window transition product counts indexed cyclic words satisfying all position tests
changed.statement:
∀ (t s : ℕ) (test : Fin (t + 1) → (Fin s → Bool) → Bool → Bool),
  let next := fun (state : Fin s → Bool) (b : Bool) (j : Fin s) =>
    if h : j.val + 1 < s then state ⟨j.val + 1, h⟩ else b
  let step := fun i : Fin (t + 1) =>
    (Matrix.of (fun p q : Fin s → Bool =>
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun bit : Bool =>
        test i p bit = true ∧ next p bit = q)).card) :
      Matrix (Fin s → Bool) (Fin s → Bool) ℕ)
  let accepts := fun w : Fin (t + 1) → Bool =>
    ∀ a : Fin (t + 1),
      test a (fun pos : Fin s => w (Fin.ofNat (t + 1) (a.val + pos.val)))
        (w (Fin.ofNat (t + 1) (a.val + s))) = true
  Matrix.trace (List.ofFn step).prod = (Finset.univ.filter accepts).card
changed.unlocks: supplies the count of walks returning to their initial state used for cyclic local constraints and the diagonal acceptance condition for their decision circuit
changed.context: Expand each matrix product entry as a count of labelled walks. Matrix multiplication sums over the joining state, and the trace counts walks returning to their starting state after k steps. A satisfying word gives state p_i[j] = w[(i+j) mod k] and label b_i = w[(i+s) mod k]. Conversely extend the walk periodically. Shifting gives p_i[j] = b[(i+j-s) mod k], so w[i] = b[(i-s) mod k] recovers the word even when s exceeds k. At width zero the state is empty and each accepted bit remains a distinct label.

Matrix multiplication sums over the joining state, and the trace counts walks returning to their starting state after k steps. A satisfying word gives state p_i[j] = w[(i+j) mod k] and label b_i = w[(i+s) mod k]. Conversely extend the walk periodically. Shifting gives p_i[j] = b[(i+j-s) mod k], so w[i] = b[(i-s) mod k] recovers the word even when s exceeds k. At width zero the state is empty and each accepted bit remains a distinct label.

changed.title: Fixing a degree-two vertex v of a graph with no 4-cycle, where G - v and G - N[v] keep an edge, saves at least three gates at false or at least four at true
changed.statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : List (Fin n × Fin n)) (v u w : Fin n) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), (∀ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ e.2) → (∀ a b c d : Fin n, a ≠ c → b ≠ d → ((a, b) ∈ E ∨ (b, a) ∈ E) → ((b, c) ∈ E ∨ (c, b) ∈ E) → ((c, d) ∈ E ∨ (d, c) ∈ E) → ((d, a) ∈ E ∨ (a, d) ∈ E) → False) → u ≠ w → ((v, u) ∈ E ∨ (u, v) ∈ E) → ((v, w) ∈ E ∨ (w, v) ∈ E) → (∀ z : Fin n, ((v, z) ∈ E ∨ (z, v) ∈ E) → z = u ∨ z = w) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v ∧ e.1 ≠ u ∧ e.2 ≠ u ∧ e.1 ≠ w ∧ e.2 ≠ w) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => x e.1 && x e.2)) → (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 3 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v false e.1 && Function.update x v false e.2)) ∨ (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 4 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v true e.1 && Function.update x v true e.2))
changed.unlocks: the 3-or-4 elimination step at a degree-two vertex, the per-vertex form
changed.context: Truth unknown to us. By exact values it holds at 312 of the 313 degree-two vertices of the checked small graphs; the one failure is the 3-path at its middle, which 'some edge avoids v' excludes (computed). Cut by the gates listing x_v in a least C: three or more readers, two readers with an AND or NOT, two OR readers, or a constant climbing two levels close by constant propagation; a lone AND reader read by an OR closes by pruning, 3 at false. OPEN: x_v's lone reader is an OR that an AND lists: the cuts give 1 at false and 3 at true. A proof there must rebuild, not only cut.

changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 16236086 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 8 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 8 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => (16236086 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C

changed.title: For r ≥ 4 and k ≥ 5r - 2, at most 2^max(floor(k/2),5r - 3) keys pass the row test at any fixed k-bit row
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : Nat), 4 ≤ r → 5 * r - 2 ≤ k → ∀ u : Fin (2 ^ k),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let h := (k + 1) / 2
  ((List.range (2 ^ k)).filter (fun w => decide (first w u.val < 2 ^ (k - h)))).length
    ≤ 2 ^ (max (k - h) (5 * r - 3))
changed.unlocks: Bounds the number of keys a row can admit in four or more rounds, for the row-side circuit construction.
changed.context: On paper. Fix u and write x = rot1(w) XOR u, a bijection. Each round reads previous offsets -1 through 3 and adds x at offset 3-2t. Inductively the left reach after t rounds is at most max(t,2t-3), the right reach 3t. At r >= 4 the tested bit i is x[p] XOR a function of x[p+1..p+L], with p=i-(2r-3), L=5r-3. Sweep the top h bits down. Each of the initial q=min(h,k-L) pivots lies outside its window and is forced by previously assigned bits. Two passing words agreeing off those q pivots coincide by induction. There are 2^(k-q) assignments off the pivots.

Inductively the left reach after t rounds is at most max(t,2t-3), the right reach 3t. At r >= 4 the tested bit i is x[p] XOR a function of x[p+1..p+L], with p=i-(2r-3), L=5r-3. Sweep the top h bits down. Each of the initial q=min(h,k-L) pivots lies outside its window and is forced by previously assigned bits. Two passing words agreeing off those q pivots coincide by induction. There are 2^(k-q) assignments off the pivots.

changed.title: For r ≥ 3 and k ≥ 7r - 1, at most 2^max(floor(k/2),7r - 2) keys pass the second test at any fixed k-bit column
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : Nat), 3 ≤ r → 7 * r - 1 ≤ k → ∀ v : Fin (2 ^ k),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let h := (k + 1) / 2
  ((List.range (2 ^ k)).filter (fun w => decide (second w v.val < 2 ^ (k - h)))).length
    ≤ 2 ^ (max (k - h) (7 * r - 2))
changed.unlocks: Bounds the number of keys a column can admit from three rounds onward, for the column-side circuit construction.
changed.context: On paper. Fix v and write z = rot3(w) XOR v, a bijection. Each round reads previous offsets -2 through 4 and adds z at offset 2-3t. Inductively the left reach after t rounds is at most max(2t,3t-2), the right reach 4t. At r >= 3 the last key supplies z[p] at p=i-(3r-2), before a window z[p+1..p+L] with L=7r-2. Sweep down the h tested bits. The initial q=min(h,k-L) pivots are fresh. Equal bits off these pivots force equal pivot bits in order for passing words. Later cyclic checks can only discard assignments. Count the 2^(k-q) choices off the pivots.

changed.title: Distances between disjoint row pairs and distinct columns bound the size of every relabelled symmetric square
changed.statement:
∀ (n m a gap : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool)
    (rowPair : (Fin m × Bool) ↪ Fin n)
    (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (kept : Finset (Fin n)),
  let rowDistance := fun (firstRow secondRow : Fin n) =>
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun col : Fin n => G firstRow col ≠ G secondRow col)).card
  let colDistance := fun (firstCol secondCol : Fin n) =>
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun row : Fin n => G row firstCol ≠ G row secondCol)).card
  let minority := fun (line : Fin n) =>
    min (Finset.univ.filter (fun onCol : Fin n => G line onCol = true)).card
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun offCol : Fin n => G line offCol = false)).card
  (∀ i, rowDistance (rowPair (i, false)) (rowPair (i, true)) ≤ a) →
  (∀ b c, b ≠ c → a + gap ≤ colDistance b c) →
  (∀ u ∈ kept, ∀ v ∈ kept, G u (π v) = G v (π u)) →
  gap * m ≤ gap * (n - kept.card) +
    ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ \ kept, minority u
changed.unlocks: the estimate for how many row and column inputs can share their sole OR reader in the explicit four-regular family
changed.context: On paper. At most b disjoint row pairs lose an endpoint when b rows are deleted. Symmetry makes matched columns of a surviving pair disagree at most a times on the kept rows, hence at least g times outside. Count by deleted row: each disagreeing column pair uses a distinct 1 and a distinct 0. A deleted row pays at most its minority count. Add g for each lost pair. Circuit-price companions cannot exist for this inequality between matrix statistics.

Circuit-price companions cannot exist for this inequality between matrix statistics.

changed.title: Joint row and column pivots give one normalized completion per (6r-5)-bit seed in the nonwrapping cyclic key test
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : Nat), 4 ≤ r → (k + 1) / 2 + (7 * r - 2) ≤ k →
  ∀ u v : Fin (2 ^ k),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let h := (k + 1) / 2
  let s := 6 * r - 5
  let seedOf := fun (w : Fin (2 ^ k)) (j : Fin s) =>
    w.val.testBit ((k - (2 * r - 2) + j.val) % k)
  let canonical := fun (w : Fin (2 ^ k)) =>
    ∀ i : Fin k, 4 * r - 3 ≤ i.val → i.val < k - h - (3 * r + 1) →
      w.val.testBit i.val = false
  let selected := fun (w : Fin (2 ^ k)) =>
    first w.val u.val < 2 ^ (k - h) ∧
      ∀ j : Fin (r + 3), (second w.val v.val).testBit (k - h + j.val) = false
  let joint := fun (w : Fin (2 ^ k)) =>
    first w.val u.val < 2 ^ (k - h) ∧ second w.val v.val < 2 ^ (k - h)
  ∃ decode : (Fin s → Bool) → Fin (2 ^ k),
    (∀ (label : Fin s → Bool) (key : Fin (2 ^ k)),
      key = decode label ↔ seedOf key = label ∧ canonical key ∧ selected key) ∧
    ((∃ raw, joint raw) ↔ ∃ label, joint (decode label))
changed.unlocks: constructs the normalized key used by the joint row and column sweep in the nonwrapping range
changed.context: On paper. For tested bit i the last key injection supplies the row pivot i-(2r-2) or column pivot i-(3r+1) alone. Trace earlier rounds to bound all other dependencies above it, no farther right than i+4r-3. Guess the 6r-5 bits above the top row pivot through the top column endpoint. Solve all row pivots downward, then the lowest r+3 tested column equations immediately below them. Zero the complement of the joint interval. Fresh pivots force uniqueness. Check the remaining column equations on the decoded key.

Solve all row pivots downward, then the lowest r+3 tested column equations immediately below them. Zero the complement of the joint interval. Fresh pivots force uniqueness. Check the remaining column equations on the decoded key.

changed.title: At most 24(k+1)²(r+1)·2^min(k,6r-5) fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates for a joint key passing two cyclic tests after r≥4 rounds
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : Nat), 4 ≤ r →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let h := (k + 1) / 2
  let graph : Fin (2 ^ k) → Fin (2 ^ k) → Bool := fun row col =>
    (List.range (2 ^ k)).any (fun w =>
      decide (first w row.val < 2 ^ (k - h)) && decide (second w col.val < 2 ^ (k - h)))
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (k + k) C ∧
    C.size ≤ 2 ^ (min k (6 * r - 5)) * (24 * (k + 1) ^ 2 * (r + 1)) ∧
    ∀ bits : Fin (k + k) → Bool,
      C.eval (List.ofFn bits) = PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) graph bits
changed.unlocks: bounds the gates for deciding whether the two cyclic tests admit a common key, including when the sweep wraps
changed.context: On paper. Guess min(k,6r-5) seed bits. With a partial word solve descending row pivots, then up to r+3 column pivots below them. Stop when k bits are assigned. If bits remain after both sweeps, neither tested block reads them. Evaluate a whole state with unknown bits zero to obtain each fresh pivot wire. Verify both tests on the completed word and OR the slots. One state costs k(4+19r) gates. At most k pivot calls and two checks per slot fit the stated budget. At width zero use an empty AND.

changed.title: Parity-equation projections preserve term width and at most double Res(k,+) refutation length
changed.statement:
∀ (V W : Type) [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq W] (k : ℕ)
    (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V))
    (H : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause W))
    (extend : (W → Bool) → V → Bool)
    (project : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.LinEq V → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.LinEq W),
  1 ≤ k →
  (∀ e, project (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.negLinEq e) =
    PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.negLinEq (project e)) →
  (∀ a e, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.LinEqSat a (project e) ↔
    PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.LinEqSat (extend a) e) →
  (∀ C ∈ F, ∃ D ∈ H, ∀ a, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.ClauseSat a D →
    PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.ClauseSat (extend a) C) →
